text: "Gluten Free Ebola" is the second episode of the eighteenth season of the American animated television series South Park, marking the 249th overall episode. It was written and directed by series co-creator Trey Parker and premiered on Comedy Central in the United States on October 1, 2014. The episode satirizes the gluten-free diet trend and the frequent changes to the Western pattern diet and the then-current food guide. After the events of "Go Fund Yourself," Stan, Cartman, Kyle, and Kenny return to school and are ostracized for having insulted their friends before their startup. At a staff meeting, Mr. Mackey boasts about adopting a gluten-free diet, which irritates others. To regain popularity, Cartman organizes a party for Scott Malkinson's diabetes, announcing it over local radio station WSPIC. Principal Victoria, who has been converted to gluten-free by Mr. Mackey, asks if the party has gluten-free food, to which the boys provide no answer. At the community center, a USDA scientist attempts to debunk gluten-related fears by extracting gluten from wheat dough; Mr. Mackey pressures him to drink the sample, leading to his violent death and a town-wide food panic. Cartman, panicked, calls Kyle and claims the entire town has taken all gluten-containing food, making the party impossible. The USDA works to resolve the crisis. At the Marsh home, two USDA agents find a can of beer in the garbage, which Randy dismisses as harmless—unaware that beer contains wheat—leading to his quarantine at a Papa John's restaurant with Mr. Garrison and an unnamed civilian. Stan, tasked with getting pop star Lorde to perform, tries to identify Randy’s co-worker who knows Lorde before being pushed back into Papa John's. Cartman dreams of Aunt Jemima (a parody of Mother Abigail), who tells him the food pyramids are upside-down, though Cartman misunderstands. As gluten-free toppings at Papa John's run out, the unnamed resident eats pizza dough containing gluten, believing it's a setup, and dies shortly after. At the radio station, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny cancel the party to focus on educating the public about gluten dangers. Cartman, claiming to know the solution, calls the USDA and asserts the food pyramid is upside-down. Surprisingly, the new dietary model works. The boys then host a successful party, with Stan reconciling with Wendy, who asks him to dance as the credits append "GF" (gluten-free) to a handful of cast and crew. Randy Marsh performs as Lorde at the party, foreshadowing the next episode. The episode's concept originated from Trey Parker and Matt Stone observing how people, including themselves, adopted gluten-free diets, leading them to create a satire of the trend. The A.V. Club's Josh Mordell gave the episode a C, finding the gluten-free panic "reasonably funny" but criticizing the lack of a B-story. IGN's Max Nicholson rated it 7 out of 10, praising the gluten panic but criticizing the party storyline, calling the radio segments "among the least funny South Park moments in recent memory." Spin magazine's Brennan Carley criticized the Lorde parody, questioning whether she had done anything worthy of the cartoon creators' ire; South Park responded in the following week's episode "The Cissy" with a subplot involving a Spin reporter named "Brandon Carlile" investigating the concert and stating: "It would be a shame if someone was…having fun at her expense." In January 2026, the United States Secretary of Health and Human Services, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., introduced a new food pyramid model that inverted the traditional structure, placing meats, dairy, fats, fruit, and vegetables at the top. This sparked social media claims that "Gluten Free Ebola" had predicted the pyramid inversion and that the "Make America Healthy Again" movement was merely recycling South Park jokes. In response, Kennedy's Twitter account @SecKennedy posted an edited clip from the episode showing the traditional pyramid reorganized into the 2026 model.
